advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Document or harden `push_fast_forward`'s `_UNKNOWN` branch so a failed tip re-read cannot mask a CAS mismatch (e.g. retry the ls-remote or classify the combined failure distinctly).
evidence: `tip = remote_tip(core, repo_root, ref, remote)`
`if tip == new_oid: return`
`if tip is not _UNKNOWN and tip != observed: ... raise CalledProcessError(128, ...)`
`raise core.RefLockPushError(remote, ref, result)` — reached when tip is _UNKNOWN, carrying the PUSH result's stderr not the ls-remote failure
advisory.finding: `push_fast_forward` success is decided by comparing the re-read remote tip to `new_oid` (our own unique commit) OR, for a CAS mismatch, comparing the tip to `observed`. For the legacy-blob path this function is never used (that path uses `_push_lease_cas`), but for a non-legacy chained write `old_oid` is always the observed parent commit — the comparison is sound. However, the re-read via `remote_tip` performs a second network round-trip on every rejected push; on an S3 remote a rejected push followed by an ls-remote adds latency to the already-serialized conditional-write path, and if that ls-remote itself times out it returns `_UNKNOWN`, surfacing a transport error (RefLockPushError) that hides the real CAS outcome.
scenarios: a rejected push whose follow-up ls-remote times out or errors on a flaky S3 remote

This branch is the central S3-reliability contract — a push whose reply was lost but whose commit actually landed must be reported as success, not retried/failed. No test drives a nonzero push return where the remote tip equals new_oid.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] In push_fast_forward, treat a _UNKNOWN verification tip (ls-remote failed) as a retryable/CAS-indeterminate condition for the publish retry loop rather than raising a fatal RefLockPushError.
evidence: Primary failure: the original `git push` is rejected (returncode != 0) at src/rebar/reconciler/_ref_lock_push.py:183-184.

Secondary/fallback leg: the verification read `remote_tip` runs `ls-remote` with check=False and returns `_UNKNOWN` on any non-0/non-2 exit (src/rebar/reconciler/_ref_lock_push.py:150-159) — a transient connectivity/throttle failure of the re-read.

New surfaced disposition: `if tip is not _UNKNOWN and tip != observed:` is False when tip is _UNKNOWN, so control falls to `raise core.RefLockPushError(remote, ref, result)` (src/rebar/reconciler/_ref_lock_push.py:189-200), a RefLockError subclass (src/rebar/reconciler/_ref_lock.py:79).

Old surfaced disposition: the prior `push_lease_cas` classified the ORIGINAL push stderr via `is_cas_mismatch_stderr`; a CAS-marker rejection raised CalledProcessError(128,'git update-ref',ref) which `_cas_once` maps to a CAS mismatch -> `_cas_advance` returns None (src/rebar/reconciler/_ref_lock_push.py:67-80, _advisory_lock.py:287-291).

Caller/classifier that changes behavior: `last_pass.publish` loops `for attempt in range(3)` on a FALSY `_cas_advance` return with jittered backoff (src/rebar/reconciler/last_pass.py:329-344); a RefLockPushError is not a CAS mismatch so it escapes the loop and the publication is not retried.
advisory.finding: In push_fast_forward, a rejected push whose verification ls-remote fails transiently (remote_tip returns _UNKNOWN) is raised as RefLockPushError instead of being classified a retryable CAS mismatch, so last_pass.publish's 3-attempt retry loop abandons a transient/retryable transport fault.
scenarios: S3/git-remote-s3 store where a last-pass publish push is refused and the follow-up ls-remote hits a network/throttle blip, returning _UNKNOWN.
advisory.suggested_fix: When remote_tip returns _UNKNOWN, raise the retryable CalledProcessError(128,'git update-ref',ref) shape (or a distinct transient error the publish loop retries) instead of RefLockPushError, so the verification read's own transience is not misclassified as a genuine push failure.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] In `remote_tip`, distinguish rc==0-with-no-matching-line from a true absence (return `_UNKNOWN` or assert a line matched) so a mis-parsed ls-remote fails closed rather than reading as free.
evidence: `if result.returncode != 0: return _UNKNOWN`
`for line in (result.stdout or "").splitlines(): oid, _, name = line.partition("\t"); if name.strip() == ref: return oid.strip()`
`return None` — reached on rc==0 with no matching line, indistinguishable from the rc==2 (absent) verdict
dropped.finding: `remote_tip` returns `None` (ref absent / free) when `ls-remote --exit-code` exits 0 but no output line matches the ref name. On exit 0 git guarantees a matching ref existed, so this branch is normally unreachable — but if git ever emits a differently-formatted line (e.g. a peeled `^{}` entry, or a refname with different whitespace), the loop falls through to `return None`, which push_fast_forward then treats as 'tip absent' rather than 'unknown'. An absent verdict derived from a successful-but-unparsed ls-remote cannot be distinguished from a genuinely free ref, so a mis-parse reads as free.
scenarios: ls-remote succeeds but the expected ref line is absent/unparsed from stdout
dropped.suggested_fix: When returncode==0 but no line matches `ref`, return `_UNKNOWN` instead of `None`.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm that a push rejection with an unchanged/indeterminate tip on the sync remote is genuinely non-retryable for last_pass.publish, or preserve the retryable CAS-mismatch disposition when the rejection stderr still indicates contention.
evidence: Primary failure: a concurrent writer wins and this push is refused; previously `push_lease_cas` matched the rejection stderr ('stale info'/rejected markers) via is_cas_mismatch_stderr and raised CalledProcessError(128,'git update-ref',ref) (src/rebar/reconciler/_ref_lock_push.py:67-80).

Old surfaced disposition: that CalledProcessError(128) is classified by _cas_once as a CAS mismatch -> _cas_advance returns None -> last_pass.publish retries (src/rebar/reconciler/last_pass.py:329-344).

New surfaced disposition: push_fast_forward decides by re-reading the tip; when `tip == observed` (unchanged) neither the success branch (line 186) nor the moved-tip CAS-mismatch branch (line 189) fires, so it raises RefLockPushError at src/rebar/reconciler/_ref_lock_push.py:200 — a non-mismatch error that escapes the publish retry loop.

Caller behavior change is asserted by the test edit: the retry test now injects `_advance_remote_last_pass` to actually move the remote tip (tests/interfaces/facades/test_reconciler_last_pass_heldout.py:184-193), because a rejection with an unchanged tip is deliberately 'a genuine failure, not a CAS loss' per the inline comment — confirming the retried-vs-fatal reclassification.
The publish loop otherwise raises LastPassError only after three attempts (last_pass.py:344); a RefLockPushError now short-circuits that and gives up on attempt one.
dropped.finding: push_fast_forward reclassifies a push rejection with an unchanged remote tip from a retryable CAS mismatch (old stderr-based classification) to a fatal RefLockPushError, so last_pass.publish no longer retries a losing concurrent write that reads back as unchanged.
scenarios: git-remote-s3 per-ref conditional-write contention where the losing push is refused but the winner's bundle is not yet listed, so the re-read tip reads unchanged.
Any remote that refuses a push for a reason that leaves the observed tip momentarily unchanged.
